issues.description: Global root-logger mutation in _shutdown_telemetry strips all LoggingHandler instances, not just the one this module installed.
issues.detail: _shutdown_telemetry iterates root.handlers and removes every OTLP LoggingHandler by isinstance scan. This rips out handlers installed by user code or other subsystems in embedded/multi-job hosts. Hold the handler reference returned by _setup_cloud_tracer and remove only that one. Document the re-entrant-emit-during-flush invariant inline.

issues.description: _flush_early_log_buffer discovers the OTLP handler by isinstance scan and replays into the first match.
issues.detail: If any prior OTLP LoggingHandler exists on the root logger, replay goes to the wrong sink and the real handler is silently skipped. Store the handler created in _setup_cloud_tracer on JobContext and address it by identity rather than scanning global logging state.

issues.description: _BufferingHandler.buffer is an unbounded in-memory list with no cap, byte limit, or eviction policy.
issues.detail: Between _start_log_buffering and flush/cleanup the list grows without limit. A slow hang or chatty DEBUG logging can OOM the worker before the crash path runs. Make it a bounded ring buffer (record count or bytes), drop oldest on overflow, and emit a one-line warning on flush noting any drops.

issues.description: Patch bundles unrelated worker.py race fix, makefile parallelism removal, and test changes with the crash-log feature.
issues.detail: The worker.py _pending_assignments reorder is a separate race fix; dropping -n auto and excluding test_plugin_google_stt.py is test-infra. Bundling them with the crash-log upload feature breaks bisect and revert hygiene. Split into separate commits with stated rationale for each.

issues.description: Crash-log path complects buffering, sink/recording policy, and handler discovery in _on_cleanup.
issues.detail: _on_cleanup synthesizes RecordingOptions with logs=True regardless of user/server config, while buffering lifecycle and OTLP handler lookup are smeared across JobContext, _flush_early_log_buffer, and _shutdown_telemetry. Separate the buffer (value), the upload policy (should we upload crash logs?), and the handler (reference held at install time).

issues.description: Bare except Exception around init_recording risks leaking half-initialized telemetry state.
issues.detail: The except clause catches Exception broadly, logs, and only calls _stop_log_buffering on failure. If init_recording raises after partially wiring the OTLP pipeline, half-initialized state leaks into shutdown. Narrow the catch or guarantee _stop_log_buffering runs unconditionally; also debug-log the dropped buffer length on the reentry/no-cloud path so silent drops are auditable.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the core design — buffer early logs, replay through OTLP once recording initializes, force-resolve shutdown_fut on early crash — is the right shape, but execution has two serious problems. First, both the replay path and the shutdown path locate the OTLP LoggingHandler by isinstance scan over the root logger, which is fragile and mutates global state with process-wide side effects; the handler should be held by reference. Second, the in-memory buffer is unbounded and will OOM a slowly-hanging worker. The patch also bundles an unrelated worker.py race fix and makefile/test changes that should be split. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK before merge — scope the handler, cap the buffer, split the patch.
